# Smoothed supporting facets: exact curvature and coupled second-order necessity

This note isolates information that is absent from the first-order smooth separator. It does not assert a sharp numerical payment. The slab identities below are unconditional. Their use at an attained smooth body minimum requires the stated actual twice-differentiable cover hypotheses; no stationary polyhedral approximation is assumed.

## 1. Exact planar slab identities

Let h>0 and let Psi be a nondecreasing CDF, zero below -1 and one above 0. Write psi=Psi' where this derivative exists, and choose the convex primitive

    J(q)=integral_(-infinity)^q Psi(s) ds.

Fix a facet patch of area A, use the signed distance x normal to its plane, and let eta be the cap margin at the old facet. The moving cap margin is x+eta-t c. In an INSIDE patch the body is x>=t v; in an OUTSIDE patch it is x<=-t v. Here v is positive for inward body motion in either case, whereas c is the threshold motion in the cap's own positive direction. Choose H so large that the remote endpoints below remain saturated for small |t|.

The corresponding captured slab masses are exactly

    F_in(t)=A integral_(t v)^H Psi((x+eta-t c)/h) dx,
    F_out(t)=A integral_(-H)^(-t v) Psi((x+eta-t c)/h) dx.

Put kappa=eta/h and W=Psi(kappa). Direct integration gives

    -F_in'(0)=A[v W+c(1-W)],
    -F_out'(0)=A(v+c)W.                              (1)

Thus the linked section selectors are 1-W inside and W outside. The first response is linear. Reversing the velocity consequently has no nonzero first-order defect at positive width.

At a differentiability point of Psi,

    -F_in''(0)=+(A/h) psi(kappa)(v-c)^2,
    -F_out''(0)=-(A/h) psi(kappa)(v+c)^2.              (2)

These signs follow from the actual captured-volume integrals, rather than from independent section and boundary allocations.

There is also a useful exact identity not requiring Psi to be differentiable. Define

    D_J(k,s)=J(k+s)+J(k-s)-2J(k)>=0.

Then

    2F_in(0)-F_in(t)-F_in(-t)= A h D_J(kappa,t(v-c)/h),
    2F_out(0)-F_out(t)-F_out(-t)=-A h D_J(kappa,t(v+c)/h).  (3)

Indeed the remote endpoint term in F_in is affine in t and cancels; the remote term in F_out is zero. If kappa stays bounded and h tends to zero with t fixed, (3) tends respectively to A|t||v-c| and -A|t||v+c|. This recovers the exact unsmoothed supporting-hinge reversal identity. Taking t to zero first instead gives the quadratic responses (2). The order of scales matters.

For the uniform outward kernel Psi(q)=min(1,max(0,1+q)), formula (3) remains exact. Formula (2) holds with psi(kappa)=1 when -1<kappa<0 and with psi(kappa)=0 when kappa lies strictly outside [-1,0]. At the two endpoints one must retain (3), or its appropriate one-sided quadratic limit, rather than assign an arbitrary value to psi.

## 2. Exact second derivative of an equalized smooth cap menu

Fix one selected source menu, with weights rho_j>0 summing to one. Along an ACTUAL scalar body path let F_j(t,b) be the captured mass of its j-th fixed-normal smoothed cap at threshold b. Assume F_j is C2 near (0,b_j), that F_j(0,b_j)=Q, and that

    -partial_b F_j(0,b_j)=S_j>0.

Suppose the actual full-fiber cover is continued by the equations

    F_j(t,b_j(t))=q(t),
    sum_j rho_j[b_j(t)-b_j]=alpha(t),                 (4)

where alpha is the ACTUAL contact minimum used by that cover and is C2, with alpha(0)=0. The implicit function theorem applies because B=sum_j rho_j/S_j>0. Let r_j=b_j'(0) and set

    K_j=F_j,tt+2r_j F_j,tb+r_j^2 F_j,bb,

with all partial derivatives evaluated at the old cap. Differentiating (4) twice gives the exact identity

    q''(0)=[sum_j rho_j K_j/S_j-alpha''(0)]/B.        (5)

Proof: the first differentiated cap equation is q'=F_j,t-S_j r_j. The second is q''=K_j-S_j b_j''; substitute b_j''=(K_j-q'')/S_j into the second differentiated budget equation.

In a planar slab contribution, -K_j is exactly the cap-loss curvature in (2), with c=r_j/|u_j| after using distance coordinates. Other terms in K_j, and alpha'', remain part of (5). In particular, a putative positive inside-facet term cannot be declared an objective descent before these terms and ALL source groups are included.

If the actual width is h Gamma_t(u), differentiating the width supplies further terms. For bounded width derivatives and bounded kappa, the leading normal-square term is still of order h^(-1) as in (2), while its cross terms with dot Gamma are bounded. This observation is only a scaling calculation; it is not a uniform bound along an arbitrary sequence of changing bodies or normal fans.

## 3. The correct coupled necessary condition

Here is a finite-dimensional statement that does not silently turn a multiple-source minimum into separate source minima.

Let U be an open neighborhood of 0 in R^m consisting of admissible actual perturbations. Suppose C2 functions f_i:U->R, i=1,...,r, satisfy f_i(0)=beta and that the actual body objective B(s) obeys

    B(0)=beta,   B(s)<=max_i f_i(s).

Assume 0 is a local minimum of B. In the application f_i is the normalized depth furnished by the actual continued cover of source i; strict off-source gaps ensure the displayed global upper bound for small perturbations.

Write g_i=grad f_i(0), H_i=Hess f_i(0), and

    Lambda={lambda_i>=0: sum_i lambda_i=1,
                              sum_i lambda_i g_i=0}.

Then Lambda is nonempty, and for EVERY direction v with g_i.v=0 for all i,

    max_(lambda in Lambda) sum_i lambda_i v^T H_i v >=0.  (6)

Proof of nonemptiness: if no such lambda existed, strict separation of 0 from the compact convex hull of the g_i would produce a vector w with g_i.w<0 for every i. The actual objective would decrease along tw, a contradiction.

For (6), consider all second-order accelerations w through

    s(t)=t v+(t^2/2)w.

The neutral-direction condition and Taylor expansion give

    f_i(s(t))=beta+(t^2/2)[v^T H_i v+g_i.w]+o(t^2).

Thus no w can make every bracket strictly negative. Separation of the affine subspace

    {(v^T H_i v+g_i.w)_i : w in R^m}

from the open negative orthant gives nonzero lambda>=0 annihilating every column (g_i)_i and satisfying sum_i lambda_i v^T H_i v>=0. Normalize its sum to one. This proves (6). Conversely, a violation of (6) yields just such a strict second-order descent acceleration by the same finite-dimensional alternative.

The multiplier in (6) may DEPEND ON v. This dependence cannot be discarded. If Lambda happens to be a singleton, its unique weighted Hessian is nonnegative on the common neutral subspace. If there is one group, g_1=0 and H_1 is nonnegative on the entire admissible signed space. Neither assertion may be applied separately to groups of a multigroup objective.

At fixed epsilon, with f_i=q_i/M, a neutral direction has q_i'=beta M' for every i. The normalized second derivative is then

    f_i''=(q_i''-beta M'')/M.                        (7)

Together, (2), (5), (6), and (7) give the precise coupled inside-versus-outside quadratic budget whenever the actual C2 path/cover hypotheses hold.

## 4. Actual scope and the remaining application

Positive-width smoothing supplies singleton deepest source groups of distinct parity and a linear first response. It does not on its own establish the C2 body/contact hypotheses used here. For a fixed stable polyhedral combinatorial family, sufficiently smooth kernel, and nondegenerate unique contact Hessian these can be verified by ordinary differentiation and the implicit function theorem, but no general attained minimizer has been shown to belong to that subclass.

Similarly, to divide a sequence of (6) by h^(-1) and retain only the supporting-facet quadratic terms requires uniform control of every remaining K_j, alpha'', and normalized-volume term on the actual sequence. Such control is not asserted here. The uniform kernel additionally requires the exact finite-difference treatment (3) at kink offsets.

The exact new invariant is therefore a conditional, globally coupled second-order necessary condition, not an established Gamma_d/2^n inequality. The common-height facet blow-up arising from the uniform kernel is a different possible mechanism; it should not be identified with or assumed to satisfy this signed C2 perturbation theorem.
